text: This service reads the GL write-off outcome, the balance facts and the freshness of each data product only through the rwb-source-data contract, publishes nothing it read from a view, and keeps the FSD field names as the source field names that contract returns.
why: Architecture v5 (higher in precedence) makes the 30 views readable by rwb-source-data alone and gives the S7 row one REST call, to P1.
read: FSD S7 validation rules and integration points as a statement of which facts the scan, the decision and the posting need, not of how they are read.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 1; Section 6 FR-S7-001, FR-S7-002; Section 8.2; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S7-01
confirm: Solution architect with P1, before wave 4 system test
impact: If a view stays readable by this service, the boundary test and the freshness guarantee would each need a second owner.

text: The posting decision, the posting reference, the rejection, the retry and the re-post are this service's behaviour, and the posting itself is obtained as a step on rwb-payment's queue with the GL outcome read back through the source-data contract; this service writes no posting entry and calls ALS or the general ledger on no path.
why: Architecture v5 slide 20 puts postProceeds in S7's OUT as a payment child and gives S7 the GL outcome by REST from P1, and slide 28 makes the write-off posting wait for the ledger.
read: FSD A2.9 as the posting behaviour the business needs, with the posting execution read as P8's capability.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 5 CAP-S7-009; Section 6 FR-S7-023, FR-S7-029; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S7-02
confirm: Solution architect with the P8 owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: Two writers of one posting would make the approved-against-posted reconciliation meaningless.

text: This service owns the four entity groups Architecture v5 names (eligibility, committee, posting, recovery after charge-off) in schema rwb_writeoff, the table write_off keeps the name and the eleven fields the Ownership Map and the Logical Data Model give it, and no other physical table name is stated because the map lists none.
why: Architecture v5 slides 20 and 41 give the schema and the four groups; the map and the model hold one table.
read: Architecture v5's list of what the schema holds as the entity set, with the physical names of the other three left to the DB story.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 10.4; Section 12 OQ-S7-03
confirm: Data architect, before the S7 DB story
impact: The migration and the boundary test cannot be written until the table set exists; the story that creates it is not blocked.

text: The write-off collection operations are published under /api/recovery/writeoff/v1, the two operations the Ownership Map holds keep their paths, and the collection paths slide 20 names are added to the contract before the contract story closes.
why: Slide 20 and slide 41 name the collection paths; the map and the API specification hold only the scan and the committee-decision operations.
read: Slide 20's IN line as the operation set the screen and the committee need, with the register entries to follow.
applied_in: Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S7-04
confirm: Solution architect, before the S7 contract story closes
impact: Without the collection operations the screen has nothing to call and the committee has nothing to submit to.

text: The provision inputs and the tax file reach Finance through the rwb-integration contract, with the retry and the task after the retry limit held here; no file is produced or delivered by this document's design.
why: The program BRD makes P2 outbound-only and gives it the file windows, and the FSD requires the feed on the month-end close.
read: FSD A2.10 and R-WO-26 to R-WO-28 as the feed the business needs, with the delivery read as P2's interface.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-010; Section 6 FR-S7-027; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S7-05
confirm: Solution architect with the integration lead, before wave 4 system test
impact: Finance cannot close the month on a feed with no owned path, so the release is blocked, not the build.

text: The pack document is held in the document hub and this service holds its reference and its retention class, read and written through the P5 contract; the closure test on a missing retention class is answered by that contract.
why: The document hub is the system of record for recovery documents and carries JOB-17 retention, and the FSD names it as the integration point of the pack.
read: FSD A2.3 as a requirement on the pack's content and evidence, with the storage read as P5's capability.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-003, CAP-S7-013; Section 6 FR-S7-010, FR-S7-039; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S7-06
confirm: Solution architect with the P5 owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: A pack held in two places would let the committee approve one document and the retention test check another.

text: The agency instruction, the result, the recall and the replacement travel through the rwb-partner contract and the partner portal, and the placement slices are sequenced last inside wave 4 because S9 is created in the same wave.
why: R-WO-30 to R-WO-35 name the portal for the instruction, the result and the recall, and the program BRD places S9 in wave 4.
read: FSD A2.15 and A2.16 as the placement behaviour the business needs, with the channel read as S9's portal.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-015; Section 6 FR-S7-033, FR-S7-034; Section 9; Section 10.3; Section 12 OQ-S7-07
confirm: Partner and agency manager with S9, before wave 4 system test
impact: If the portal is not ready inside the wave, the placement is demonstrated last and the rest of the release is unaffected.

text: A charged-off population is handed to the debt sale route of rwb-debtsale with the population, the route and the approval recorded here, and the case closes when the buyer settles and the data transfer completes.
why: R-WO-32, R-WO-50 and R-WO-51 give this module the hand-over and the closure on the buyer's settlement and remittance, and S6 owns the lot, the award and the transfer.
read: FSD A2.16 as the sale behaviour the business needs, with the lot and the award read as S6's capability.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-016; Section 6 FR-S7-035, FR-S7-038; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S7-08
confirm: Solution architect with the S6 owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: A sale with no recorded hand-over cannot be reconciled to the book it removes.

text: The write-off states are held as the stage's own record inside WriteOffWorkflow, this service publishes the outcome on rwb.writeoff.events.v1, and rwb-case moves the case state because it owns the case and the parent workflow.
why: Architecture v5 gives the case state and the parent CaseWorkflow to rwb-case and gives this service one published event.
read: FSD and Business Rules S7 state machine as the stage's decision record, with the case state read as P3's.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-013; Section 6 FR-S7-040; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S7-09
confirm: Solution architect with the P3 owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: Two writers of the case state would make the closure and the reopening control unprovable.

text: JOB-16 runs as a Temporal Schedule in rwb-writeoff on the 3rd working day that also tests that the ALS batch is complete, and no Quartz table, connection or job is used; the Ownership Map ruling on JOB-16 (ASM-A6-flows-12) is carried, not reopened.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 and the Temporal design make it a Schedule; the Batch and Scheduling Design starts it on the batch record and the design's Phase 1 note keeps Quartz.
read: Both conditions as one product requirement: the date the business runs on and the data the rules require.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 6; Section 6 FR-S7-003; Section 9; Section 12 (no open question; ruled)
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 4 system test
impact: A scan that runs on a date without a complete batch would propose a population on stale data.

text: The eligibility and tax rules are read from a governed package through the rwb-decision contract, the package and rule version are recorded on every scan and decision, and the package code and promotion date are taken as open because they are Phase 2.
why: All fifty-one rules are versioned data evaluated in process, and the design states that the package codes are Phase 2 with this service as one owner.
read: R-WO-01 to R-WO-51 as the rule set, with the package identity read as P7's governance.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 7; Section 5 CAP-S7-014; Section 6 FR-S7-007; Section 10.4; Section 12 OQ-S7-14
confirm: Center of excellence analyst with P7, before wave 4 release
impact: A scan that cannot name its package cannot be defended to tax or to audit.

text: The tax criteria and the two tracks are held as a versioned package read at run time, the version is recorded per account, and the scan is held on a published version only; no criterion and no track name is asserted here.
why: No source read defines the criteria, and the epic BRD carries the same gap as Q-006 with ASM-013.
read: FSD A2.2 as a requirement that the criteria exist as data with a version, with the values left to their owner.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-002; Section 6 FR-S7-004, FR-S7-005, FR-S7-006; Section 12 OQ-S7-10
confirm: Write-off committee member, before wave 4 release
impact: The scan can be built and tested against a test package; the release is blocked until the real one is published.

text: The write-off exception loop is owned by the write-off team role until a named owner is decided, and it carries one time limit as a data row rather than a code constant.
why: The FSD states the loop has no owner today and the epic BRD carries Q-007 with ASM-014 reading it as the write-off team.
read: ASM-014 as the interim owner, with the time limit as a value nobody has stated.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-012; Section 6 FR-S7-030; Section 12 OQ-S7-11
confirm: Head of recovery, before wave 4 release
impact: Without an owner and a limit the loop repeats the finding that its cases do not close.

text: No write-off cap value, basis or period is asserted, and the population is reported against the cap only once the cap exists; the committee limit of R-WO-11 and R-WO-12 is the only limit this release enforces.
why: RISK-004 names the cap as undecided and no requirement, rule or field carries it.
read: The risk as a statement that a cap is expected, not as a value.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S7-007; Section 10.4; Section 12 OQ-S7-12
confirm: Head of Asset Liquidity with Risk, before wave 4 release
impact: Enforcing a guessed cap would hold a population the policy does not require and misstate the headroom.

text: The committee approval is taken through the approval workflow on rwb-decision, the limit is read from the delegation table at run time, and the level applied and the approver role are recorded; the level values are loaded from the regulation under DL18 and the committee composition is taken as open under Q-001.
why: Architecture v5 makes the approval an ApprovalWorkflow child with the DoA lookup as a parameter, and the limits are DL18.
read: FSD A2.5 and A2.6 as the decision the business needs, with the level values read as policy data.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-005, CAP-S7-006; Section 6 FR-S7-015, FR-S7-016, FR-S7-020; Section 12 OQ-S7-13
confirm: Risk with the product heads, before wave 4 release
impact: A decision taken at the wrong level is an authority breach that the record would then prove.

text: The write-off posting is a point of no return under strict mode: it waits for rwb-decision to confirm the decision record in the central ledger, proceeds only on that acknowledgement, and raises an alert where the ledger is late.
why: Architecture v5 slide 28 lists the write-off posting among the four irreversible steps, and the Temporal design repeats it.
read: FSD A2.9 as the posting behaviour, with the ledger acknowledgement added from the higher-ranked architecture.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 9; Section 6 FR-S7-029; Section 11 AC-S7-015; Section 12 (no open question; constrained)
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 4 system test
impact: A posting on an unconfirmed record is the one error an auditor cannot unwind.

text: A retention class and a retention period are held as data on every document and every record this service closes on, the closure is held when a class is missing, and the periods themselves stay open under DL26 and Q-012.
why: NFR-031 sets the closure after the retention period with the target not set, and NFR-028 leaves the periods open.
read: The closure control as a requirement, with the period read as Compliance's data.
applied_in: Section 7 NFR-S7-014 to NFR-S7-018; Section 6 FR-S7-039; Section 12 OQ-S7-15
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 4 release
impact: A closure with no period recorded cannot be defended at a data subject request or a disposal audit.

text: write_off carries the eleven fields of the Logical Data Model, the three GL-sourced ones are marked as mirrored and never re-keyed, and DEF-05 is taken as open because no source read defines it.
why: The FSD defers the mirrored GL fields to DEF-05 and lists eight fields; the model holds eleven.
read: The model as the field set, with the FSD's eight as the subset the screen needs.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 12 OQ-S7-17
confirm: Data architect, before the S7 DB story
impact: A missing field would either re-key the GL coding or lose the recovery position.

text: The removal reason, the review date, the decision reason and the pack reference are required fields of the eligibility and committee records, held with the physical names the DB story fixes.
why: Four rules act on those values and neither the FSD catalog nor the model holds them.
read: The rules as the source of the fields the behaviour needs.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 6 FR-S7-011, FR-S7-018, FR-S7-019; Section 12 (carried in OQ-S7-03)
confirm: Data architect, before the S7 DB story
impact: Without the fields the removal, the deferral and the refusal cannot be recorded or proved.

text: The pack is drafted by the write-off agent through the rwb-agent contract under the agent-run template with a 60-second limit and the template pack as the fallback, and the pack itself is the product requirement rather than the agent.
why: R-WO-05 names the write-off agent, the agent runtime is P10, and the matrix gives S7 no P10 cell.
read: FSD A2.3 as a requirement on the pack's content, with the draft read as P10's capability.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-003; Section 6 FR-S7-009; Section 9; Section 12 (carried in OQ-S7-01 and OQ-S7-06)
confirm: Solution architect with the P10 owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: A pack that depends on an agent with no fallback stops the committee when the agent is slow.

text: A payment after charge-off is matched by rwb-payment and reaches this service as ProceedsMatched; this service records the recovery, the income and the agency fee, and shows a payment that matches nothing in its own exception list.
why: P8 owns payment and proceeds matching and publishes ProceedsMatched to rwb-writeoff, while R-WO-37 to R-WO-39 give the matching to this module.
read: FSD A2.15 as the recovery behaviour the business needs, with the initial match read as P8's capability.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-015; Section 6 FR-S7-036, FR-S7-037; Section 9; Section 12 (carried in OQ-S7-02)
confirm: Solution architect with the P8 owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: Two matchers of one payment would double-count a recovery or leave it unmatched.

text: Completeness is published from rwb-reporting, fed by the decision record and WriteOffApproved, and the reconciliation itself stays in this service; no extract to a data lake and no Power BI copy is created.
why: R-WO-42 names Power BI and Architecture v5 removes the data lake and the extract (ADR-018).
read: The completeness control as a requirement, with the channel read as P9's read model.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S7-011; Section 6 FR-S7-028; Section 9; Section 12 (carried in OQ-S7-02)
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 4 system test
impact: A control published nowhere is a control nobody reads.

text: SCR-27 is served through a gateway-bff composite route that joins this service's population and pack answer with the case and the document, and no service is named as the screen's owner in this document.
why: Architecture v5 makes gateway-bff the only entry for staff screens and DP-19 makes the screen a composite route.
read: FSD Screens as the screen the business needs, with its ownership read as the edge's.
applied_in: Section 9; Section 12 (carried in OQ-S7-04)
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 4 release
impact: A screen owned by nobody has no release, no test and no accessibility sign-off.

text: This version is Draft and its approval table stays empty: no Product Owner decision and no FDA decision exists for the BRD or the FSD this PRD is built from, so no approval is claimed.
why: The FSD is 'In review' with an empty sign-off table, and no approval record for either document was found in the sources read.
read: A Draft PRD is a reviewable document; an approval recorded without a decision would be a false record.
applied_in: Section 1.1; Section 13
confirm: Product Owner, before the requirements gate
impact: The gate stays open until both roles decide, and every downstream stage inherits the open status.

text: All release dates are copied unchanged and marked tentative: E3 31 January 2027, E4 28 February 2027, E5 31 March 2027, E6 30 April 2027, E7 31 May 2027 and E8 30 June 2027, with wave 4 covering EP06 to EP08.
why: U7 and DL48 fix the dates as unchanged and tentative, and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: The program release plan and the wave map as the schedule, with no date computed here.
applied_in: Section 1.1; Section 10; Section 11.3
confirm: Product Owner, at each release planning point
impact: If a date moves, the slices of section 10 are re-cut and no requirement changes.

text: Every owner named in this document is a role or a service code from the Ownership Map or the BRD; no person is named, and the owners in the delegate tables are roles to be filled.
why: Rule 4 of the run and U3 of the story rules forbid the name of a person anywhere.
read: The BRD role list and the Ownership Map service codes as the only owner vocabulary.
applied_in: Section 3; Section 9; Section 11.3; Section 13
confirm: Product Owner, before the requirements gate
impact: A named person in a document is a maintenance defect the moment that person changes role.
